title: Alexandr Wang wanted to make Meta 'cool again' — and memes were part of his plan
key_facts: Alexandr Wang, 29, Meta's chief AI officer, said in a recent interview with podcaster David Senra that he posted memes about Muse, Meta's personal AI assistant, on X.
He said the posts were meant to make Meta "cool again" and that "the internet rewards risk".
He said the posts "actually made an impact on growth"; no figures are given.
Muse launched on 8 Sep and reached the top of Apple's app store 10 days later, surpassing ChatGPT, per Business Insider.
Meta says Muse can research, fill out forms, buy items, book restaurants and connect to email, calendars, Spotify, Instagram and OpenTable.
Business Insider says Muse is Meta's first successful breakthrough in AI after its Llama and Spark models failed to find niches.
quote_evidence: "It actually made an impact on growth," he said of the posts, "which is kind of hilarious."
In his interview with Senra, though, Wang said that his often spur-of-the-moment posts served a broader goal — to make Meta "cool again."
After launching on September 8, Muse shot to the top of Apple's app store 10 days later, surpassing ChatGPT.
why_it_matters_hint: A senior Meta executive links a deliberate meme strategy to Muse's growth, but gives no numbers.
event_date: Interview described as recent, date not stated; Muse launched 8 Sep 2026
notes: Interview itself (podcast) not opened; Business Insider relays Wang's words.
